summary_md:
## The author's five notes

1. **The repeated explanation in the argument:** change {tag:argument}.
2. **What Silas was checking:** in the same group.
3. **Explanations in the fight:** changes {tag:fight}.
4. **Sentence rhythm in the calmer descriptions:** changes {tag:rhythm}.
5. **The ship's reveal:** changes {tag:ship}.

changes.title: The title
changes.before: # Chapter 6
changes.after: # Chapter 6 – The Words of the Dead
changes.why: The author chose the title from 25 options on 30 September. It follows Chapters 1–5 in shape and works twice: the ogre's copied words, learned from people it caught, and Gerolt's words ("the old fool" in a neighbour's mouth, and the instruction Alaric is following).

changes.title: Alaric's grievance, not a repeat
changes.before: "Then tell me that. You wouldn't tell me anything about her, and then you said you were taking the sword and I had to wait outside."
changes.after: "Then why couldn't you tell me what you were doing? You said you were taking the sword and I had to wait outside."
changes.why: The author: Silas had already explained the danger to the inn before Alaric left ("And if they're watching the inn?…"), so "Then tell me that" blurred Alaric's real grievance. He was told about the danger; he wasn't told the arrangement or why Silas was going. "How was I meant to know that? You said, 'We'll see.'" stays.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: What Silas was checking
changes.before: "There's a way along the south wall. That's what I was checking. When we get there, I'll have a look at the inn. If it's clear, we both go in, and you show her the sword yourself. If there are riders, we wait. All right?"
changes.after: "There's a way along the south wall. I was checking how we could get there. When we do, I'll have a look at the inn. If it's clear, we both go in, and you show her the sword yourself. If there are riders, we wait. All right?"
changes.why: The author: they haven't reached the town yet, and Alaric couldn't even see it from the rise, so "That's what I was checking" suggested Silas had inspected the wall from somewhere without a view. He knows the town already; he was checking their approach to it. "When we get there" became "When we do" so "get there" isn't said twice.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: Cut the explained swing
changes.before: It brought him in towards its mouth. He saw the tusks and the wet teeth between them, and he twisted round and swung the sword at its face, at anything, because otherwise he was going into that mouth. The blade hit something. It dragged, and caught, and tore free.
changes.after: It brought him in towards its mouth. He saw the tusks and the wet teeth between them, and he twisted round and swung the sword at its face, at anything. The blade hit something. It dragged, and caught, and tore free.
changes.why: The author: we've just watched it bring him towards its open mouth, so the desperate swing already says why.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: Let the failed attempts carry it
changes.before: When he could turn his head, he saw Silas on the slope above him, and the ogre between them with its back to Alaric now. Blood was running down the arm Silas had cut, and down its face from the cheek Alaric had cut, and dripping off both. It had no club. It was grabbing at Silas with its open hands, and Silas gave ground up the slope with his blade held out in front of him. He couldn't get in. Every time he tried, a hand came at him, and he had to go back again, and the leaves slid under him. One hand caught his cloak and dragged him half off his feet before he tore free.
changes.after: When he could turn his head, he saw Silas on the slope above him, and the ogre between them with its back to Alaric now. It was grabbing at Silas with its open hands, and Silas gave ground up the slope with his blade held out in front of him. Every time he tried to get in, a hand came at him, and he had to go back again, and the leaves slid under him. One hand caught his cloak and dragged him half off his feet before he tore free.
changes.why: The author: the paragraph explained both wounds and said Silas couldn't get close, then showed his attempts failing. Kept the failed attempts and the sliding footing. The club's absence is still visible in its "open hands", after the reader has seen the club drop.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: Holding, not pinned
changes.before: Silas was still there, against it. His feet were sliding. He had it pinned to the tree, and it was pulling at the blade and at him, and he didn't let go.
changes.after: Silas was still there, against it. His feet were sliding. He was holding it against the tree, and it was pulling at the blade and at him, and he didn't let go.
changes.why: The author: "pinned" sounds more secure than the struggle described.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: Vary the rhythm: the ogre
changes.before: It was bigger sitting than Silas was standing. Its skin was a dirty white all over, and its gut hung over a band of rags tied round its middle, and two tusks came up out of its lower jaw on either side of its mouth. There was a club across its knees, a whole branch with the bark still on, studded with spikes. It turned its head towards the barking, slowly, until it was facing straight up the slope at him.
changes.after: It was bigger sitting than Silas was standing. Its skin was a dirty white all over. Its gut hung over a band of rags tied round its middle, and two tusks came up out of its lower jaw, one on either side of its mouth. Across its knees lay a club, a whole branch with the bark still on, studded with spikes. Slowly, it turned its head towards the barking, until it was facing straight up the slope at him.
changes.why: The author: the run of "and…and" suits the capture and the fight, where things arrive faster than he can take them in, but it also ran through the calmer descriptions. Details get their own sentences here; the paragraph stays long.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: Vary the rhythm: Kelmend
changes.before: It lay at the bottom of the slope, across fields gone grey in the dusk. There was a wall round it, and roofs inside the wall, and smoke going up from a great many chimneys. Outside the wall, all along the near side of it, there were more roofs, lower and closer together, pressed right up against the stones. A road ran across the fields to a gate, and there were still people on it, a cart and a few more on foot, all going in. Lights were coming on in the windows, and on top of the wall somebody was walking along lighting torches, one after another.
changes.after: It lay at the bottom of the slope, across fields gone grey in the dusk. A wall ran round it, with roofs crowded inside and smoke going up from a great many chimneys. Outside the wall, all along the near side of it, there were more roofs. They were lower and closer together, and pressed right up against the stones. A road ran across the fields to a gate, and there were still people on it: a cart, and a few more on foot, all going in. Lights were coming on in the windows. On top of the wall, somebody was walking along lighting torches, one after another.
changes.why: The author's rhythm note, as for the ogre.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: One "last of the light" fewer
changes.before: He let himself sit down on the grass. Wena lay down beside him with her head on her paws. A dog was barking somewhere down in the town, and Wena's ears lifted at it and then dropped again. The wind came up the slope smelling of chimney smoke and of somebody's supper, and Alaric was hungry again. Behind the town, the last of the sun was going.
changes.after: He let himself sit down on the grass. Wena lay down beside him with her head on her paws. A dog was barking somewhere down in the town, and Wena's ears lifted at it and then dropped again. The wind came up the slope smelling of chimney smoke and of somebody's supper, and Alaric was hungry again. Behind the town, the sun was going down.
changes.why: The author: "the last of the light" sat in neighbouring paragraphs; with the reveal tightened, this keeps the sunset without the echo.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: One introduction for the ship
changes.before:
Something was coming out of the last of the light beyond the town.

At first it was only a shape against the last of the light, too big to be anything, and he couldn't tell how far off it was. Then it was over the wall, and the torches along the top of it were tiny underneath, and still it came on, and the hum grew until he could feel it in his teeth.

The shape overhead kept growing. Alaric found the bow, then the dark red plating behind it, and the spines beneath. Blue-green light ran along its underside.
changes.after:
Beyond the town, against what was left of the sunset, there was a shape too big to be anything. He couldn't tell how far off it was. Then it was over the wall, and the torches on top looked tiny beneath it. The hum grew until he could feel it in his teeth.

It kept growing. Alaric found the bow, then the dark red plating behind it, and the spines beneath. Blue-green light ran along its underside.
changes.why: The author: the shape was introduced three times ("Something was coming…", "At first it was only a shape…", "The shape overhead kept growing…"). The progression was already there: the hum, a distant shape, the wall tiny beneath it, the plating and the light, then overhead. Now it's introduced once, with separate sentences for the steps. *Pass 2:* "the top of it… beneath it" pointed two ways.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: Vary the rhythm: overhead
changes.before: It went over them. The hum filled everything, and the blue-green light slid across the grass and across Wena, flat against Alaric's legs, and across Silas's upturned face, and then it was past. Down on the wall, the torches had stopped going on and started moving.
changes.after: It went over them. The hum filled everything. Blue-green light slid across the grass, and across Wena, flat against Alaric's legs, and across Silas's upturned face. Then it was past. Down on the wall, the torches had stopped going on and started moving.
changes.why: The author's rhythm note. The light's sweep stays one sentence; the hum and its passing get their own.
changes.decision_note: The author's review of the first draft, 30 September.

changes.title: A repeated phrase
changes.before: Once, a bird clattered up out of the bushes beside the path, and Wena threw herself against Alaric's legs, and he had the sword up before he knew it. It was only a bird. His heart took a long time to believe it.
changes.after: Once, a bird clattered up out of the undergrowth beside them, and Wena threw herself against Alaric's legs, and he had the sword up before he knew it. It was only a bird. His heart took a long time to believe it.
changes.why: Claude's check: "the bushes beside the path and" was also where Wena found the deer. An objective repeat, so fixed in this round; the author can reject it.

changes.title: Unwinding the cloth once
changes.before: Silas sat down on the slope beside him and started unwinding the cloth from the burned hand. It had gone brown and black where the hilt had been, and it stuck.
changes.after: Silas sat down on the slope beside him. The cloth round his burned hand had gone brown and black where the hilt had been.
changes.why: The author's optional trim: this paragraph and the next ("Alaric watched him pull the loosened cloth away from his hand.") both described him unwinding it. Now the first shows the cloth and the second the pulling.
changes.decision_note: The author, 30 September: "minor polish, not something that warrants another revision round".

changes.title: The morning's already gone
changes.before: The slope was steep, and his legs were heavy from the river and the whole morning behind them, but he climbed it faster than he'd walked all day. Nobody was ahead of him deciding where he went. It felt good, and he let it.
changes.after: The slope was steep, and his legs were heavy from the river and the long walk, but he climbed it faster than he'd walked all day. Nobody was ahead of him deciding where he went. It felt good, and he let it.
changes.why: Pass 1: It's past midday by now (the farm was "near midday"), so "the whole morning behind them" was wrong.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for three passes for errors, inconsistencies and POV slips (30 September).

changes.title: Which tree
changes.before: Alaric tried to stand. His ankle gave, and he caught himself against the tree.
changes.after: Alaric tried to stand. His ankle gave, and he caught himself against a tree.
changes.why: Pass 1: "the tree" was the one the dead ogre was slumped against.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for three passes for errors, inconsistencies and POV slips (30 September).

changes.title: Where the sack is
changes.before: Silas poured water from the skin over it without a sound, and took a fresh strip of cloth out of the sack.
changes.after: Without a sound, Silas poured water from the skin over it, then nodded at the sack by Alaric's feet. Alaric found a strip of clean cloth in it and passed it across.
changes.why: Pass 1: Silas took the cloth out of the sack himself, then said "Give me the sack" as though Alaric had it. Now the sack is by Alaric's feet, where Silas dropped it, and Alaric passes the cloth, so the line works.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for three passes for errors, inconsistencies and POV slips (30 September).

changes.title: Which way out of the hollow
changes.before: They went down out of the hollow and up the far side of it. Every step downhill jarred Alaric's ankle. After the first few he gave up trying to keep up and just walked, and Silas was never far ahead. Silas had slowed down. He didn't say so, and Alaric didn't either.
changes.after: They went back down into the hollow and up its far side. Every step downhill jarred Alaric's ankle. After the first few he gave up trying to keep up and just walked, and Silas was never far ahead. Silas had slowed down. He didn't say so, and Alaric didn't either.
changes.why: Pass 1: The fight was on the near slope, between the hollow and the rise. They go back down into the hollow, not out of it.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for three passes for errors, inconsistencies and POV slips (30 September).

changes.title: The way in
changes.before: Silas was looking at the wall. "Once it's dark. If the wall's quiet, we go round to the south side, and I have a look at the inn."
changes.after: Silas was looking at the wall. "Once it's dark. If it's quiet, we go down along the south wall, and I have a look at the inn."
changes.why: Pass 1: The south gate is already the nearest end, so "round to the south side" didn't fit. It now matches his "a way along the south wall". *Pass 3:* "the wall's quiet… along the south wall" put the wall in the same line twice.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for three passes for errors, inconsistencies and POV slips (30 September).

changes.title: Which "it" came away
changes.before: Its head jerked back. Its other hand let go of the club, and the club dropped into the leaves, and it clapped the hand to its face. When it came away, blood was running out of a split in its cheek, just under the eye. It shook him, roaring, and the trees and the sky and the ground swung round and round, and Alaric held on to the sword with both hands.
changes.after: Its head jerked back. Its other hand let go of the club, and the club dropped into the leaves, and it clapped the hand to its face. When the hand came away, blood was running out of a split in its cheek, just under the eye. It shook him, roaring, and the trees and the sky and the ground swung round and round, and Alaric held on to the sword with both hands.
changes.why: Pass 2: "When it came away" could have meant the ogre.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for three passes for errors, inconsistencies and POV slips (30 September).

changes.title: Hand, then a hand's width
changes.before: Alaric grabbed Wena's collar and pulled her back. His ankle gave way under him, and he fell in the leaves right beneath it, with Wena on top of him, and a hand came down at them: the one he had cut, with the blood running off the back of it. It missed his face by a hand's width and raked the ground beside his head.
changes.after: Alaric grabbed Wena's collar and pulled her back. His ankle gave way under him, and he fell in the leaves right beneath it, with Wena on top of him, and a hand came down at them: the one he had cut, with the blood running off the back of it. It missed his face by a few inches and raked the ground beside his head.
changes.why: Pass 2: "a hand came down… by a hand's width" in the same breath.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for three passes for errors, inconsistencies and POV slips (30 September).
